notes.title: 🎮 Gamepad Support is Coming to Steel Swarm: APOCALYPSE!
notes.content:
In Steel Swarm: APOCALYPSE, the war is no longer limited to just mouse and keyboard! Very soon, gamepad support for Xbox, PlayStation, and other controllers will be available on Windows systems.  
Whether you're ambushing in the city or dodging under Mantis’ feet — now you can do it all while chilling on your couch, gamepad in hand.

[list]
[*][b][h3]🕹️ More Control, More Fun[/h3][/b]

With the new gamepad support:

[list]
[*] Xbox, PS, and other controllers will be [b]plug & play[/b] compatible.
[*] Menus and UI will be optimized for controller navigation.
[*] To match the console-style gameplay, [i]aim assist[/i] and [i]streamlined driving[/i] features will also be enabled.
[/list]

This means a smoother and more competitive experience, especially for players who prefer to play with a controller.
[/list]

[list]
[*][b][h3]👀 Ready to Feel the Console Spirit?[/h3][/b]

This update isn’t just about comfort — it's a signal of what's to come.

As many console players already know:

[i]Some battles just feel better with a controller.[/i]

Which makes us wonder:

[quote]"Could Steel Swarm come to consoles someday?"[/quote]
[/list]

[list]
[*][b][h3]📅 When Is It Coming?[/h3][/b]

Gamepad support is currently in its final testing phase and will be [b]released very soon[/b].

Be sure to follow our social media and Steam page so you don’t miss the announcement!

[b]Steel Swarm: APOCALYPSE[/b] keeps evolving.  
Whether you're a seasoned commander or a brand-new pilot — the fight is now at your fingertips.

And this time, [b]the aim is yours… and so is the throttle.[/b]

[b]SSA Team[/b]
[/list]

notes.title: Developer Spotlight: Serdar Oygen
notes.content:
At [b]Clay Token[/b], our software development engineer [b]Serdar Oygen[/b] shares the challenges he faced while developing [b]Steel Swarm: Apocalypse[/b], the best advice he received in software engineering, and how he stepped out of his comfort zone in this project. 🚀

[b]🔹 Can you briefly introduce yourself?[/b]  
I've been working as a software development engineer at Clay Token for about 1.5 years. I love listening to music and outdoor sports.

[b]🔹 What music genres and bands do you listen to while developing?[/b]  
I can't write down a long list here, so let's just say I pick whatever comes to mind at the moment and go with it.

[b]🔹 What is the best piece of advice you’ve received about software development?[/b]  
I’d like to share this quote (unfortunately, I don't know the source, so I can't give proper attribution):  

[quote]There are two types of software engineers: those who understand computer science well enough to do challenging, innovative work, and those who just get by because they’re familiar with a few high-level tools.  

Both call themselves software engineers, and both tend to earn similar salaries in their early careers. But Type 1 engineers progress toward more fulfilling and well-remunerated work over time, whether that’s valuable commercial work or breakthrough open-source projects, technical leadership, or high-quality individual contributions.  

Type 1 engineers find ways to learn computer science in depth, whether through conventional means or by relentlessly learning throughout their careers. Type 2 engineers typically stay at the surface, learning specific tools and technologies rather than their underlying foundations, only picking up new skills when the winds of technical fashion change.[/quote]

[b]🔹 What was the most challenging bug you encountered in this project, and how did you solve it? Also, what was your last "developer panic moment," and how did you handle it?[/b]  
A [b]build automation script[/b] was silently crashing every once in a while, and I couldn’t find what was wrong for a long time. Eventually, I had to implement a [b]preventive measure[/b] to detect silent crashes and do whatever was necessary.

As for my [b]developer panic moment[/b], while people were waiting to join a test match, I accidentally [b]killed one of our backend services[/b]. Unfortunately, there was no quick fix. People just had to wait until I got the service running again.

[b]🔹 What’s something you did in this project that pushed you out of your comfort zone, and you’re glad you did?[/b]  
When I first started with the project, I was assigned [b]gameplay-related tasks[/b], and there were many aspects that challenged me. [b]Using different systems instead of what the game engine provided[/b] helped me step out of my comfort zone and learn new things.

Over time, as my tasks grew in scope, I found myself [b]spending a lot of time outside my comfort zone[/b]. In my opinion, for someone at an early stage in their software engineering career like me, [b]staying in a comfort zone doesn’t mean much.[/b]

[b]🔹 What are you currently learning? How do you prioritize your "next things to learn" list?[/b]  
Right now, I’m reading essays by [b]Fred Brooks[/b]. As the scope of my work expands, I find myself needing to explore the [b]social aspects of software engineering[/b]. After this, I’ll move on to topics that will require me to [b]get under the hood and do low-level stuff.[/b]

When deciding what to learn next, I focus on a few key things:  
[list]
[*] First, I have a [b]main goal[/b] for what I want to achieve.  
[*] Then, I choose [b]smaller objectives[/b] that contribute to that goal.  
[*] As I learn and gain new insights, I adjust my learning path accordingly.  
[/list]

Sometimes, I [b]pause[/b]. Sometimes, [b]imposter syndrome kicks in[/b]. I don’t see these as failures, just [b]part of the process[/b]—another reason why I don’t rigidly stick to a priority list. I don't see these things as black and white, which is why I find the idea of a [b]"strict priority list"[/b] a bit rigid. So, I can’t give a definitive answer here.

[b]🔹 How many cups of coffee do you drink per day?[/b]  
Zero. The cliché of programmers and their love for coffee will remain [b]a cliché[/b] for me.

[b]🔹 What advice would you give to a newly graduated developer?[/b]  
[b]Don’t turn every piece of advice you receive into a personal problem just because you lack experience.[/b]  
This is [b]your journey[/b]—walk your own path.

[b]🔹 Among the features you developed in this project, which one makes you the proudest and why?[/b]  
I take pride in any [b]feature that increases efficiency, remains functional for a long time, adapts to new needs with modifications, and is easy for my teammates to use.[/b]

notes.title: SSA – Drastic META Change?
notes.content:
[b][h2]SSA’s 2025_1_3: Major Balancing Patch[/h2][/b]

SSA’s 2025_1_3 is the first major balancing patch of 2025. Although it may seem modest, there may be large consequences to the game’s core mechanics. Let’s take a look…

[b][h3]The following two are critical:[/h3][/b]

- [b]All minions' HP has been reduced by 25%.[/b]  
- [b]All vulcans' damage has been reduced by 25%.[/b]  

Experienced players will notice that these changes will [b]increase the overall lane-pushing speed[/b] in the game.  
This effect will be even stronger in [b]empty lanes.[/b]  
We also expect this to [b]increase the amount of xalium gained, especially in the early game.[/b]  
This effect may differ slightly from [b]XBT to XBT,[/b] which may force us to rebalance in the future.

[b][h3]Equally important is the change in the "XP reward formula for XBT Kills":[/h3][/b]

- The base experience points gained from [b]XBT kills[/b] now change according to the level of the XBT.

Experience points gained from XBT kills in the early game could cause a [b]small snowball effect, especially in low-ELO matches.[/b]  
In order to prevent this and reduce the luck factor, we decided to determine the base XP reward according to the level of the killer XBT.

[b]Important Note:[/b]  
If you kill a higher level XBT than yourself, you still earn more XP, and if you kill a lower level XBT, you earn less XP.  
There has been no change in the XP change formula according to the [b]level difference between players.[/b]  
However, this formula is now combined with the base XPs. [b]In other words, the increased risk due to the level difference is now rewarded more.[/b]  
This gives the player who has fallen behind a nice chance to catch up.

[b][h3]Gear System Changes[/h3][/b]

[h4]Stun Immunity:[/h4]  
- Duration reduced from [b]30 seconds[/b] to [b]10 seconds.[/b]  
We heard you CC users and significantly reduced the effect duration of your nightmare [b]"Stun Immunity".[/b]  
Now timing will be much more important when using this gear.

[h4]Xalium Stealer:[/h4]  
- Life steal amount has been [b]doubled.[/b]  
- Price has been changed from [b]3000[/b] to [b]2500.[/b]  

[h4]Counter Fire:[/h4]  
- Damage amount has been [b]increased by 4x.[/b]  

These two gears had become very unpopular with the recent nerfs.  
We have significantly increased their effects. However, [b]we are still keeping an eye on this dangerous duo.[/b]  
There may be changes in the future.

[h4]Shield:[/h4]  
- Price reduced from [b]2250[/b] to [b]1250.[/b]  

We think this [b]silent but effective gear[/b] can be a good option for the early game.  
We have made its price more attractive to encourage users.

[h4]Bug Fixes:[/h4]  
- Fixed some damage and buff skills not breaking invisibility when used.  

Yes, we noticed that some very effective skills that were supposed to cancel invisibility did not.  
[b]We apologize to our commanders[/b] who fell victim to treacherous ambushes exploiting this bug, and we are fixing it with this update.

[b][h3]Those are the important balance changes in SSA's 2025_1_3 patch.[/h3][/b]  
We wish all our players a balanced and enjoyable 2025!
[b]
SSA TEAM[/b]
